More than a decade ago, filmmaker Roberto Reid started work on a documentary about the Tates. Though that film was never made, Toxic Empire features interviews with Reid, as well as footage that he shot as far back as 2015. “Even back then, I could see the potential trajectory of Andrew Tate and where he was heading,” Reid says in the doc.

entertainment.title: Cardi B and Offset See Beverly Hills Mansion Lawsuit Dismissed After Settlement
entertainment.summary: The estranged couple was accused of filming Cardi B’s “Like What” music video at the iconic mansion under the guise of shooting a TikTok clip
entertainment.body:
The lawsuit accusing Cardi B and Offset of duping the owner of a Beverly Hills mega-mansion into letting them film a music video for her song “Like What” for a discounted TikTok video rate has been dismissed after the parties reached a confidential settlement, a source and court documents obtained by Rolling Stone reveal.

A source confirmed the parties reached a settlement “subject to confidentiality.” The private pact came after both sides told a judge in April they were open to mediation and just weeks before a trial set to begin Jan. 5. Lawyers for both sides did not provide comment when contacted by Rolling Stone .

When property owner Bi LLC first sued in 2024, it claimed Cardi B, born Belcalis Almánzar, and her estranged husband, whose real name is Kiari Cephus, had their eyes on the striking glass-and-aluminum mansion once occupied by Justin Bieber and “devised a plan” to use it “without paying full market value.” The owner alleged the couple’s representatives anonymously booked the mansion “under the false pretense” that it would be used for a TikTok video. Cardi and Offset then showed up and made the property’s “distinctive architecture” the “centerpiece” of a full-length music video, the lawsuit claimed.

Cardi fired back on X , formerly Twitter, the same day the complaint was filed, saying the lawsuit was riddled with inaccuracies. “We paid those people $10,000 IN CASH to rent the property for a whole 24 hours that same day 6am to 6am the next morning and we went over by ONE hour which we paid overage fees to the realtor for in March,” she wrote. The “Money” singer added that the property “had cameras all over” and both the realtors and the owners were present “the ENTIRE time.”

entertainment.title: Director Peter Berg Isn’t Giving Up on the Unreleased Rihanna Documentary: ‘Keep Hope Alive’
entertainment.summary: The director said in 2023 that he spent six and a half years filming the project.
entertainment.body:
Remember the Peter Berg-directed Rihanna documentary that was announced way back in 2016 , and was reportedly sold to Amazon for $25 million in 2019?

During a conversation with Complex published on Wednesday (Nov. 25), Berg — who also directed the singer and business mogul in 2012’s Battleship — discussed the doc’s current status. “There’s always hope. Keep hope alive,” he said of the unreleased documentary. “If and when it does [come out], it’s going to be a banger.”

He was talked about why he thinks the nine-time Grammy winner hasn’t done more movies, and he commended the “We Found Love” singer’s ability to always make the right decision. “Rihanna does what she wants to do. She follows her heart. She follows her creative instincts,” Berg told the publication. “When she did Battleship, she was really interested in seeing what being in a big, wild Hollywood action movie was like. And then she went and made a bunch of great albums and now she’s raising a beautiful family. I guarantee you she’s going to be back in music and it’s going to be a banger.”

Berg and his team spent years recording and piecing things together for the documentary about the star, but it’s ultimately up to Rihanna whether she wants to release it eventually. He said as much in 2023 when talking with The Hollywood Reporter . “It’s done and sold, and Amazon’s ready,” the director told the outlet at the time. “She’s a perfectionist, so we keep adding. It’s been six and a half years of filming, so, yeah, it’s ready to come out. We’re just waiting on her to say, ‘Yeah, let’s do it.’ I don’t know. Maybe it’ll be a 10-year project.”

Rihanna most recently starred in 2025’s animated film Smurfs , lending her voice to Smurfette. The last live action movie she starred in was Amazon Prime’s Guava Island opposite Donald Glover , though she makes a cameo in Ali G: Who Iz I? , which arrived in October.

This week, it’s all GTA (with a little CMAs), as we look at revived favorites from Carly Rae Jepsen and The Cars, an ascendant hit from an all-star cast, and a best new artist winner at age 47 . Related Dolly Parton to Receive CNN Heroes Legacy Award, Miley Cyrus to Accept on Her Behalf ESSENCE Festival of Culture Moving On From New Orleans After Three Decades: 'Memories Were Made -- And So Was History' Noah Kahan Caps Epic Year With 'Live From the Great Divide' Album

It’s one of the most beloved pop songs of the past 15 years — but never one of its biggest chart hits. Carly Rae Jepsen ‘s “Run Away With Me” became a cult classic almost immediately upon its single release (from her enduring E • MO • TION album) in 2015, but Billboard Hot 100 success totally eluded it in its moment. (In 2023, Billboard named it the 21st greatest pop song of the Hot 100 era to never reach the chart.) But in 2026, a great pop song still has a chance to reach the Hot 100 no matter when it was originally released — and “Run Away With Me” now has the best opportunity it’s had in a decade, thanks to the release of Grand Theft Auto VI .

“Run Away With Me” plays in the record-breaking new game during a scene when its dual protagonists, Jason and Lucia, are enjoying the Vice City high life after the latter’s release from prison. With its cinematic sax and propulsive synth-pop shuffle making it an ideal soundtrack for just about any action-packed sequence, the song has become one of the breakout musical moments from the game’s heavily music-focused universe — and led many pop fans to wonder if it could result in the storied track finally reaching the Hot 100 for the first time.

The song’s streaming breakout has unquestionably been real: It was pulling daily official on-demand streams in the low 20,000s in the days before the game’s release, but that number had broken six digits by Sunday (Nov. 22, three days after GTA VI ‘s release), and was all the way up to 281,000 by Monday, according to early data provided by Luminate. That’s a gain of nearly 1,100% over the total the song posted last Wednesday, just before the game’s release, but it’s still a little low for a streaming-driven-song on the Hot 100.

The question is if the song can continue its viral growth throughout this week, and maybe even into next week. It’s got a bit of a late start for this tracking week, which runs through Thursday — and as of Tuesday, the song still wasn’t streaming enough to enter the daily top 200 on either Spotify or Apple Music — so its best chance of breaching the chart might come next week, especially if it continues to grow and then stays stable, with daily U.S. streaming numbers more in the 500k-600k range.

entertainment.title: U.K. Hard Techno Brand Teletech Is on Track to Sell 500,000 Tickets This Year. Here’s How It Broke Into America
entertainment.summary: The Manchester-born global party brand hosts a show at Space in Miami on Friday (Nov. 27) and a 20,000-capacity event in San Francisco on Jan. 2.
entertainment.body:
Anton Stevens couldn’t get booked as a DJ in Manchester, so he threw his own party. That event is now on track to sell 500,000 tickets this year.

Teletech, the hard techno party brand founded in Manchester by Stevens and Tom Shelton , has spent the past five years building a brand that functions less like a promoter and more like a scene with a passport. By the time Teletech shows up in a new city, a significant portion of the crowd is usually already wearing the event’s merch and streaming music from its label, Teletech Records. For many attendees, the experience of going to a local Teletech show is like having their favorite artist come to town.

“A lot of it comes down to the community,” says Stevens. “When we come into a market…people are already unintentionally part of our community. They’ve been listening to music on our label, buying the merch, watching the content online. When we come to town, it feels like a bigger occasion, a gathering of a community they’ve been part of from the outside that they can now be part of from the inside.”

That inside has gotten very big, very quickly. With Teletech now operating across Europe, South America, Australia and the U.S., Stevens and Shelton say the event is expected to sell close to 500,000 tickets in 2026 alone. The next few weeks will also be major, with Teletech throwing a party at Space Miami on Friday (Nov. 27) (the lineup includes Adrián Mills, Benwal, Danyelino and Hannah Laing) and a massive New Year’s event called Fresh Start in San Francisco on Jan. 2. There, artists including Sara Landry , I Hate Models and Nico Moreno will play for a crowd of roughly 20,000 at The Warehouse on the city’s Pier 80. This CV is particularly impressive given that Teletech is run by a team of five.

The brand’s origins go back to Stevens’ time at university, when he started his own club night, calling it Teletech. Around the same time, he began managing the booking calendar at the Manchester club Hidden. He eventually crossed paths with Shelton, who was finishing his studies and looking to book dance shows. The pair worked together at Hidden for years, cutting their teeth in clubland and making their names in the scene.

The pandemic was a clarifying moment. With events on pause, Stevens and Shelton spent the downtime planning a run, Stevens says, of “larger than life techno shows.” The result was XXL, a large-format techno touring brand that launched its first run — Birmingham, Bristol and Manchester on the same weekend, starting the first Friday out of lockdown — with Amelie Lens headlining. The Manchester leg was co-produced with the city’s revered dance music institution The Warehouse Project, an early sign that Teletech could work well with established brands while maintaining its identity.

entertainment.title: ‘All of a Sudden’ Is the Rare Movie That May Change Your Life
entertainment.summary: The filmmaker behind 'Drive My Car' returns with a long, gentle look at a friendship between a healthcare worker and a terminally ill playwright that brims with humanity
entertainment.body:
We go to the movies for any number of reasons: to laugh, to cry, to care ( bless you, Nicole Kidman ), to be thrilled or scared or see if Spider-Man makes it out of a scrape with a supervillain alive. The notion that we might be drawn to films so we can listen to other people talk — to be not just voyeurs but eavesdroppers — isn’t usually one of the top reasons for spending a lot of time sitting in the dark and staring at shadows on a screen. It’s a show-don’t-tell medium.

Still, there are a handful of auteurs who excel at making the art of conversation seem everything from enthralling to downright cinematic. Tarantino loves letting his characters digress at length in between violent set pieces and gratuitous shots of feet. The work of French writer-director Eric Rohmer is synonymous with long sequences of people doing nothing more than chatting about intellectual matters great and small. (His work also gave us one of the all-time great 1970’s cine-disses .) If Louis Malle had made nothing but My Dinner With Andre, he’d still be considered canon-worthy. Richard Linklater, Jean Eustache, Whit Stillman — all first-rate movie conversationalists. And then there’s Ryusuke Hamaguchi.

As anyone who’s seen the Oscar winner Drive My Car and Happy Hour — his 2015 magnum opus that clocks in at a little over five hours, and frankly could have sustained itself for twice that running time — will tell you, the Japanese filmmaker can take extended scenes of discussion and turn them into the sort of exchanges that make you lean forward. If anyone could make a connect-the-dots presentation about capitalism, healthcare, and burnout cycles scrawled onto a whiteboard in real time feel absolutely compelling, it’s him. That happens to be the centerpiece of his latest drama All of a Sudden, an ironic title for a masterwork intent on taking its time and giving its characters plenty of space to ruminate. The end result is all the better for it, too. This is the type of movie that prizes philosophical pursuits over pulse-pounding chases, and the spark of communicating ideas over crass spectacle. It’s admittedly not for everyone. For filmgoers who find two human beings connecting over reflections on life, death, art, and caretaking, however, Hamaguchi’s astounding ode to empathy as an emotional foundation for coexistence is nothing short of manna. entertainment.title: A+E Doubles Down on Microdramas With Snips Partnership (Exclusive)
entertainment.summary: The media brand is working with the company to adapt traditional entertainment projects into mobile-first vertical stories, with episodes no more than two minutes long.
entertainment.body:
A+E is deepening its investment in the world of microdramas , most recently by inking a content partnership with the shortform video company Snips, The Hollywood Reporter has learned.

Under the auspices of the agreement, Snips will use its proprietary technology to adapt previously released television programs into mobile-first stories told in vertically oriented, short chapters, with cliffhangers galore, any extraneous material trimmed and episodes no more than two minutes long. The deal will allow the mobile app to stream roughly 50 true-crime and reality projects from A+E Global Media ’s library in this shortform format.

“A+E Global Media has built some of the most obsessively watched unscripted and scripted storytelling in the industry for over four decades, and true crime and documentary content is some of the most naturally suited to how people actually watch on mobile — in short, sharp, story-driven bursts,” Snips co-founder and CEO Or Ben Shimon said in a statement . “We are delighted to bring some of A+E’s proven titles into our growing catalog.” The specific titles that will be adapted for the Snips audience were not immediately available.

The Snips deal will provide A+E, which will retain ownership rights over projects, with data on viewership, completion rates, monetization and engagement for specific titles on the app. Meanwhile, the projects provided by A+E will augment the entertainment library available on Snips, which now includes around 1,700 titles.

A+E Global Media is no stranger to the microdrama format, having first dipped its toes in the space in March when its label Lifetime released the project Tides of Temptation , executive produced by Taye Diggs. The company and Lifetime announced in October that they are releasing additional microdrama projects on MyLifetime.com and the Lifetime mobile app. A+E further revealed that it had adapted nearly 200 of its own projects into microdramas that the company would license to third-party platforms.

Snips has previously partnered with Banijay Rights and BIG Media to distribute microdrama adaptations of the latter companies’ projects.

“The idea of Snips, it’s to be a platform. We’re not creating our own content because we don’t want to compete with our content partners,“ Ben Shimon said in an interview with The Hollywood Reporter. “The idea for us is that we’re building relationships first [with] adapting content. Second, [our content partners] think about testing things or testing new genres with us.”

entertainment.title: Brandi Carlile Slams ICE for ‘Horrific’ Detainments in Seattle: ‘We Need to Do Something About It’
entertainment.summary: The singer encouraged fans to donate to organizations protecting immigrants and demand action from representatives.
entertainment.body:
Brandi Carlile is joining the outcry in her home state of Washington following the controversial ICE detainments of two people at Seattle-Tacoma International Airport.

In a Tuesday (Nov. 24) joint statement posted on Instagram alongside her Looking Out Foundation , the country singer-songwriter began by writing, “I, along with many of you, have seen the horrific video this week of a father and daughter being violently detained by ICE agents at the Seattle Airport.”

“The horror and heartache I experienced watching this, hearing their cries of desperation and fear, cannot be overstated,” she continued.

The video in question showed masked, unmarked ICE officers forcefully handling Ricardo Larrondo Mendoza on the floor as he and daughter Sofia Hernandez Mejia were boarding a plane on their way to a family baptism in California. Both were taken into custody, with the DHS telling Billboard in a statement that they’d “overstayed” their visas.

“Ricardo and Sofia were travelling to be with their family,” Carlile wrote. “Many of us will be doing the same in the coming weeks as we gather with those we love for the holidays. The ability to do so safely, to have a home we can return to, to have the freedom of movement and travel without fear is one we all deserve. That right is being threatened across the U.S. every day for immigrants and their families and we need to do something about it.”

The musician ended by encouraging followers to “channel our distress into action” by either donating to the Looking Out Foundation’s Our Neighbor’s Fund or contacting government representatives to “make your feelings known.”

Carlile isn’t the only musician who’s condemned ICE for the airport incident. Seattle band Pearl Jam also released a statement , criticizing the organization’s “cold cruelty” and “inhumane treatment” of Mendoza and Mejia.

The Seattle Times reported that both Mendoza and Mejia arrived in the U.S. from Mexico legally with tourist visas in 2015 and applied for citizenship within a year of entering, citing their attorney.

entertainment.summary: The reality star died in August in New Jersey, with his family revealing at the time that his passing was "sudden." De Nino was 40.
entertainment.body:
“Married at First Sight” star Ryan De Nino reportedly died of the combined adverse effects of cocaine and fentanyl.

The New Jersey Department of Health shared with TMZ on Wednesday that the reality star’s cause of death also includes cellulitis, bacterial endocarditis and bacterial pneumonia.

Cellulitis, per Mayo Clinic , is a “spreading skin infection,” while bacterial endocarditis is defined as “life-threatening inflammation of the inner lining of the heart’s chambers and valves.”

Bacterial pneumonia, meanwhile, is a lung infection that can be caused by “bacteria, viruses and fungi.”

His manner of death was ruled an accident, according to the outlet.

De Nino died in August at 40, with his family revealing at the time that his passing was “sudden.”

His ex-wife, Jessica Castro, sent her “sincere condolences” to her former spouse’s loved ones, more than a decade after they wed on Season 2 of the Lifetime show.

entertainment.body:
Leila Cobo, Billboard ‘s co-chief content officer, joins Jay Wheeler at some of the most meaningful places in his life in Miami, presented by Lexus. The artist talks about the faith and family that inspire him, his beginnings and his journey to becoming “La Voz Favorita.” He also shares how he’s building his new tour, what connecting with fans through streaming means to him, and the legacy he hopes to leave behind.

Leila Cobo: Miami, a cultural explosion of diverse rhythms and home to some of the biggest stars of Latin music. I’m Leila Cobo, co-director of content at Billboard , and today, behind the wheel of the first Lexus TZ, I explore how music can be born from our values and connect deeply with people, just like Jay Wheeler does, one of my favorite artists, who today invites us to tour the places that marked his story and discover how he became the favorite voice of reggaeton. This place is important to you, right?

Jay Wheeler: Very important. The most important place, truly. The reason why I am what I am right now is because of my mom’s prayers. She taught me from a very young age there. But now that I’m grown, I understand it was worth all the times my mom told me: “You have to pray if you want things to go well.” And all that is very important, truly. Having God present in my life and in my heart will always be very important. The first time I saw my mom cry because I was doing a performance, I was playing and I saw her sitting over in this corner. She was crying because she saw me playing piano, and it moved her.

So, when you cross that threshold, you stop being an artist and become Jay Wheeler, just another parishioner of this church.

I think that from the moment I get off the stage or leave the studio, from the moment music is no longer involved, I stop being Jay Wheeler. I said that when I make music, I want to reach people’s hearts. So that’s why I started making Christian music, romantic music, music that reached the heart, heartbreak music, sad music, music that, when people listened to it, they’d say, “You helped me, you saved me, but I can’t listen to your songs because I have to cry.” I wanted to connect with people like that. So, people who know me, of course, now they know me for a bunch of other things I do, like podcasts, streaming, my daughter, my wife, my relationship. But the one who knows me deeply, the number one fan, will tell you: “Oh, yeah, Jay Wheeler is the one who sings romantic.”

entertainment.title: Bowen Yang, Mark Ruffalo and the Rise of Antisemitism in Hollywood
entertainment.summary: Recent comments from the SNL veteran and the progressive Marvel star reveal the extent to which celebrities' criticism of Israel has merged with hoary old prejudices against Jews.
entertainment.body:
Bowen Yang insists that he didn’t know “Zio” was an antisemitic slur .

In a resurfaced clip from his Las Culturistas podcast, the comedian muttered the term under his breath at the mention of Regina Spektor , the Jewish American singer-songwriter. Yang was responding to a guest, another alleged wit named Edy Modica, who said that Spektor was “a little Israel, hard-core.” Spektor, who was born in the Soviet Union and immigrated to the United States as a child refugee, has been outspoken in her defense of the Jewish state since the Hamas massacre of Oct. 7, 2023, and given her personal history, is well attuned to left-wing antisemitism . When protestors interrupted one of her concerts last year screaming “Free Palestine ,” a visibly frustrated Spektor announced to the crowd, “The only reason I even speak English is because I came here to escape this shit.” Related Stories Movies Takashi Miike's 'Bad Lieutenant: Tokyo' From Neon Gets Early 2027 Release Lifestyle Veruschka, Mesmerizing Supermodel of the 1960s and '70s, Dies at 87

“Zio,” short for “Zionist,” was popularized by former KKK Grand Wizard David Duke when he was going through a respectability phase and needed a way to attack Jews without actually naming them as such. In his apology, Yang seemed sincerely shocked to hear this. “I want to genuinely apologize for using a word on the podcast without knowing its antisemitic history,” he wrote on Instagram. “Particularly upsetting to realize that I adopted language popularized by far-right movements whose rhetoric we should be wary of and act against.”

We should take Yang at his word that he didn’t know the antisemitic etymology of “Zio.” Why would he? So profoundly antisemitic are the progressive cultural spaces Yang inhabits that people toss around racial slurs propagated by men in white hoods without a second thought. Does anyone really believe that Bowen Yang knows the first thing about the Israeli-Palestinian conflict? Like everyone in his social set, one that dominates large swaths of the entertainment world, he acquires his progressive worldview — to which vicious hatred of Israel is central — by osmosis. If there’s one issue that unites the far left and the far right in this country, it’s the Jewish Question.

Yang seemed more distraught about the far-right origins of “Zio” than he did about the community the word intends to harm: Zionists, i.e. anyone who believes in the right of Israel to exist, i.e. the vast majority of the world’s Jews. In the minds of Yang and others of his ilk, progressives cannot be antisemitic, just as they cannot be anti-black, anti-woman, anti-gay, or anti-anybody. Bigotry, to them, is exclusively a right-wing phenomenon. Yang isn’t an antisemite, you see, he’s just an “anti-Zionist.” We know this because he ended his apology with the requisite “Free Palestine,” no expression of contrition over Jewish pain complete today without a nod to the movement that wants to eliminate the world’s only Jewish state.

entertainment.body:
Logo text Neon has dated Bad Lieutenant: Tokyo from Japanese auteur Takashi Miike for a March 5, 2027 theatrical release.

The sequel Bad Lieutenant: Tokyo stars Lily James and Godzilla vs. Kong ’s Shun Oguri in a new take on the seedy and corrupt detective who first appeared in Abel Ferrara’s 1992 original neo-noir crime drama with Harvey Keitel as the Lieutenant. That was followed by Werner Herzog ’s 2009 film Bad Lieutenant: Port of Call New Orleans , starring Nicolas Cage and Eva Mendes.

Neon acquired the U.S. rights to Miike’s third franchise outing that centers on a Tokyo cop (Oguri) steeped in gambling debt and a drug addiction and paired with an FBI agent, played by James, to search for a missing politician’s daughter (Liv Morgan) in Tokyo’s Yakuza criminal underworld. Related Stories Lifestyle Veruschka, Mesmerizing Supermodel of the 1960s and '70s, Dies at 87 TV 'Top Gear' Sets 2028 Return -- With Gordon Ramsay as Host

The bad lieutenant and the FBI agent as they partner up are, without their knowledge, under the watchful eye of a crazed killer following their every move. The Neon film is written by Daisuke Tengan and is based on the original IP first produced by Edward R. Pressman.

Japanese maestro Miike is best known for movies like Audition , the Yakuza trilogy Dead Or Alive and thriller Ichi The Killer , along with Sukiyaki Western Django, Visitor Q, 13 Assassins and his 100th film, Blade of the Immortal. Miike also has an upcoming slasher-horror film starring Charli xcx, Milly Alcock, Norman Reedus, Kiko Mizuhara and Show Kasamatsu.

Bad Lieutenant: Tokyo had a world premiere at the Toronto Film Festival and will hit theaters on the same weekend as Pixar’s Gatto and Michael Jordan’s new take on The Thomas Crown Affair. The film is a US-Japan co-production, produced by the late Jeremy Thomas for Recorded Picture Company, Sam Pressman for Pressman Film, Naoaki Kitajima for Nippon TV and Misako Saka for OLM.

entertainment.title: The Country Song About Losing Your Virginity That Became an Enduring Hit
entertainment.summary: Three decades ago this week, Deana Carter sang about sex that’s as sweet as “Strawberry Wine” in a Number One country radio hit
entertainment.body:
A song about getting ditched for a Texas woman might be leading the charts right now, but, 30 years ago, Deana Carter was offering a different take on romance: the enduring, nostalgic ache of that first love. Or, if we’re being a little less polite, losing your virginity to a college guy next to a river.

The Matraca Berg and Gary Harrison-written hit “Strawberry Wine” went to Number One on country radio in November 1996, and was a seminal part of a female-dominated wave where the genre’s women could push the boundaries of what exactly they were singing about, and how they were singing it. It still resonates.

A softly-delivered ballad, “Strawberry Wine” wasn’t as outwardly bold as songs like Loretta Lynn’s “Rated X,” or deeply topical like Dolly Parton’s “Down From Dover.” Instead, it’s a wistful reflection on a teen girl’s first love, with a hair of melancholy — and how thinking back on pangs of pleasure can hit as deep in the gut as a good country song. Carter never specifically details exactly what happened between her and this summer fling, but it’s pretty clear what she’s talking about: “love growin’ wild,” “the loss of my innocence,” intoxication, being plucked from the vine before entirely ripening.

As the first single from her album with the equally boundary pushing title Did I Shave My Legs for This , Carter offered a quiet, cheeky reclamation of how subtly or overtly women could sing about sex. And not just sex: sex that comes before, and has nothing to do with, marriage or domestic life, completely devoid of the male gaze.

Carter was 30 when “Strawberry Wine” became a hit, later in life as far as the industry standards for women generally go. A Nashville native, she grew up around music through the eyes of her father, guitarist Fred Carter Jr., who appeared on records by Bob Dylan, Simon & Garfunkel, and Willie Nelson. Carter wrote most of the songs on her debut, but found that “Strawberry Wine” “just nailed my life story, which ended up being everyone’s first experience [with love],” she said in an interview for CMA’s ‘90s Country Forever . She was particularly drawn to the work of Berg, one of the genre’s strongest and boldest talents, unafraid to pitch songs about female experiences to women willing to sing them. entertainment.summary: Jewels Sparkles as Kim Kardashian as Allura Grant? Oh yes. The writer/director of All's Fair takes TVLine inside Season 2's drag queen fantasy episode.
entertainment.body:
Hulu Add TVLine on Google: Preferred Source Google Discover If "All's Fair" was a classic daytime soap opera, Season 2, Episode 6 might begin with the announcer telling viewers: "the roles of Allura, Emerald, Dina, Liberty, and Carr will now be played... by drag queens."

Appropriately titled "Queens," the gender-bending bottle episode (now streaming on Hulu) recasts the ladies of Grant, Ronson, and Greene with famous drag queens, following HR director Reese's realization that her new co-workers have more in common with the cast of "RuPaul's Drag Race" than they do with everyday, ordinary women. To Reese, this explains so much about the ladies' behavior — from their casually diabolical reads, to their outrageous fashion and beauty looks. This revelation results in one of the most entertaining psychotic breaks in recent memory, with Reese spending an entire episode imagining the lawyers in all their glamazon glory.

According to Charles Rogers, who wrote and directed the fever dream of an episode, casting the queens was largely up to series co-creator Ryan Murphy, who knew right away that he wanted New York City icon Lady Bunny to play Glenn Close's Dina. The show also did some "chasing" to land Bob the Drag Queen as Niecy Nash-Betts' Emerald, and the rest of the cast fell into place from there: Marcia Marcia Marcia as Naomi Watts' Liberty, Daya Betty as Sarah Paulson's Carr , and Olivia Lux as Teyana Taylor's Milan.

"It was crazy the way each one of them was not only was perfect for the role, but also took it so seriously," Rogers tells TVLine. "Everybody was ready to treat this, not like the drag episode of 'All's Fair,' but like they are the leads of 'All's Fair.' I just had the absolute most magical, creative, warm time with all of them. It was one of the most positive creative experiences of my entire life."

Do keep one thing in mind, though: what you see happening in this episode isn't actually happening in reality. Rogers classifies this as a "bottle episode," explaining that it's paying homage to a classic TV trope where a character has an hour-long dream sequence, whether it's from being in a coma, having a dream, or experiencing a psychotic break. To put it more simply, "what Reese hallucinates for the entirety of that episode is not canon to the show," Rogers explains.

Hulu Charles Rogers is proud of everyone's performances in the episode, but when forced to play favorites, he points TVLine to Jewels Sparkles' impressive portrayal of Kim Kardashian's Allura.

Schafer opened up about her career to date in a candid interview with Backstage , explaining that, now that "Euphoria" is over, she's starting a new chapter. "This is something I've been thinking about a lot recently, because I'm in this new moment of my life," she said, adding, "I can be more picky about what I do now, so I'm really only doing things that make me feel sparkly inside."

Amazon Prime Video While Hunter Schafer has played some pretty demanding roles in the past, stepping into the skin of Cora for "Blade Runner 2099" was her biggest challenge yet in terms of action. She talked about the physical aspect of the role in an interview with Entertainment Weekly . "It was a big lifestyle change, honestly, filming this," said Schafer. "Because it was just so much movement every day, and being on your feet, and running out of breath, and throwing yourself over objects or under or on them."

Schafer added that she was a smoker at the time and that made things even more difficult, but being able to learn from co-star Michelle Yeoh (who began her career in martial arts films in Hong Kong) made things easier. In that same interview, Yeoh revealed that she told the show's stunt coordinator to build Schafer's scenes around her instead of trying to make her do things that seasoned action actors would do. entertainment.title: Veruschka, Mesmerizing Supermodel of the 1960s and ’70s, Dies at 87
entertainment.summary: People like her “don’t go away at all,” photographer Franco Rubartelli said. “They stay in a picture, in a perfume, in a song, in a way of smiling.”
entertainment.body:
Veruschka, the chameleonic, long-limbed supermodel and performance artist who photographer Richard Avedon once pronounced “the most beautiful woman in the world,” has died. She was 87.

Veruschka died in her home in Berlin, the German newspaper Bild reported.

On Instagram, her former partner and photographer Franco Rubartelli acknowledged her death and noted “she wasn’t just a great model. She was an elegant woman, sensitive, brave, with a beauty that did not stay in the camera, it would get into the soul of whoever watched her. Related Stories Lifestyle "Sometimes You Just Have to Think: 'What Will Make People Laugh?'": Lolly Adefope on Gags, 'Ghosts' and Her West End Debut Movies Ava DuVernay to Receive London Critics' Circle Inaugural Laura Mulvey Female Trailblazer Award

“She had a way of being in the world that you don’t learn; you take in. People like Veruschka don’t go away at all. They stay in a picture, in a perfume, in a song, in a way of smiling.”

One of the first supermodels, Veruschka in the 1960s and ‘70s appeared often on covers of Vogue and other magazines around the globe. With a high forehead, blue-eyed gaze and sculptured, distinctive cheekbones, she stood more than six feet tall and was a muse for designers including Karl Lagerfeld , Yves Saint Laurent and Valentino .

“What made the German model so mesmerizing was her seeming disinterest in preserving any one iteration of that beauty,” Anna Cafolla wrote in Vogue . “She could be imperious or impish, feral or feline, androgynous or opulently feminine. She could contort her impossibly long limbs into unreal configurations, traversing fashion magazines and the wider public’s consciousness with ease in a way that had never been done before.”

Vogue offers a look at her “most striking beauty looks of all time” here .

Veruschka did her first shoot wearing nothing but body paint in 1966, and after she left modeling in 1975, she collaborated with German sculptor-painter Holger Trülzsch for a series of avant-garde self-portrait photographs in which her painted figure dissolved into forests or sides of buildings.

entertainment.body:
Stephen Wilson Jr. is having one remarkable month. The genre-blurring singer-guitarist received his first-ever Grammy nominations on Nov. 16 and quickly followed up the milestone two days later when, at 47 years old, he was named New Artist of the Year at the 60th CMA Awards.

But arguably his most high-profile recognition came just this Tuesday, when U2 revealed dates for the U.S. leg of their Greatest Show on Earth Tour: Wilson will open nine of the band’s 15 announced stadium shows. (The War on Drugs will handle the six others.)

The direct-support slot for one of the most anticipated tours of 2027 should introduce the Indiana native to a whole new audience, one that may not already know him for his indie-rock style of country music (what Wilson calls “Death Cab for Country”), his viral cover of Ben E. King’s “Stand by Me,” or the video of his quotable CMA acceptance speech that’s been making the rounds online. “I learned that the mining is the real gold,” Wilson said onstage.

Wilson’s appearance on U2’s tour also reinforces his burgeoning rock cred. In September, he performed Temple of the Dog’s “Hunger Strike” with Eddie Vedder at Vedder’s curated Ohana Fest. And earlier this month, he put his own spin on “Wonderwall” to help honor Oasis at their Rock & Roll Hall of Fame Induction Ceremony in L.A. It’s not a stretch to say that Wilson has more in common sonically with rock — or even grunge — than he does Nashville country music.

entertainment.title: Watch Nathan Fielder and Lance Oppenheim’s Full In-Depth Breakdown of ‘You Can See Everything’
entertainment.summary: The directors behind A24's unlikely powerhouse Oscar contender joined THR at the SCAD Savannah Film Festival last month, for a live Q&A about the making of the movie. You can now watch it here.
entertainment.body:
[This article contains spoilers for You Can See Everything ]

When Lance Oppenheim first told his buddy Nathan Fielder that he heard about the potential to make a new documentary about Elizabeth Holmes’ last days before going to prison, Fielder wasn’t sure what tale there was left to tell. There were other docs, books and an Emmy-winning Hulu series out there about her. “I was interested in her, but I didn’t really think there was a story there to do, especially for a doc,” Fielder said last month from the SCAD Savannah Film Festival , where he and Oppenheim joined The Hollywood Reporter for a special post-screening live Q&A (watch it in full below). Related Stories Movies 'You Can See Everything' Now Streaming: Where to Watch Nathan Fielder's Elizabeth Holmes Doc Online SCAD Savannah Film Festival David Greaves Says 'Once Upon a Time in Harlem' Is "An Act of Resistance" Against Efforts to Erase Black History

Oppenheim remembered Fielder asking, “Hasn’t there been a billion things made about this person already?” And he replied, “Yes — but maybe there’s something else.”

To say that has proven true would be the understatement of this film season. Moving in with Holmes and her partner, Billy Evans , in her final weeks of freedom — then continuing to make their movie in increasingly daring and surprising directions — Oppenheim and Fielder teamed up for You Can See Everything , one of the most successful theatrical documentaries of all time and a bona fide cultural phenomenon.

The movie offers compellingly slippery portraits of both Holmes and Evans, plays off Fielder’s noted screen persona to fascinating effect and features a plum secret role for Amanda Seyfried, who won awards for her portrayal of Holmes in The Dropout (and is now a wildcard Oscar contender). But perhaps most fundamentally, it’s a singular synthesis of what Fielder and Oppenheim have brought to their work over their last several years, toying with true-story formats in projects as diverse as Primetime and The Rehearsal .

“I feel like the two of us are both interested in the challenges of capturing authentic life on camera,” Oppenheim said. “He’s coming at it from a different angle, and I’m coming at it from a different angle too.”

Their SCAD Docs to Watch conversation finds the two directors going in-depth on their process from beginning to end on You Can See Everything — including the conversations that led to Seyfried’s participation and the biggest questions they’re still wrestling with, months after completing the movie.

entertainment.title: Police Say Unknown Substance at Don Toliver Concert Could Be Linked to Arena Robberies
entertainment.summary: The Greater Manchester Police have officially lifted the scene but the investigation continues
entertainment.body:
The Greater Manchester Police have officially lifted the scene at Manchester’s Co-op Live arena, where a Don Toliver concert was evacuated after an “unknown substance” was released into the crowd.

The investigation is still ongoing but police announced Wednesday that the substance — and its aftermath — could be linked to a string of robberies reported in the arena. According to Assistant Chief Constable Tom Harding, there were nine separate reports of jewelry theft during the concert. No arrests have been made so far, but police are continuing their work.

“We are aware similar robberies have been reported at two European concerts for the same artist and will be linking in with our European counterparts to better understand the wider picture of this suspected offending,” Harding said in a public statement. “We’ll also continue to work closely with the venue and local authority partners over the coming weeks as events begin to return to the Co-Op Live arena.”

The incident occurred at Toliver’s Sunday show at Co-op Live arena. Roughly 30 minutes after the start of the concert, witnesses reported a “horrible smell” moving through the arena, with some concertgoers “screaming,” “choking,” and “coughing up blood,” the BBC reports. Around 12,000 people were safely evacuated, 80 were treated for eye irritation, and one person was taken to the hospital for further treatment.

sports.title: Steelers suddenly have a major mess
sports.summary: The Steelers need to figure things out, immediately.
sports.body:
Lauten serves as the team’s senior director of communications. He’s basically in charge of P.R. And the Steelers have a P.R. mess unlike any they’ve ever experienced.

The benching of Rodgers has prompted a predictable reaction. Rodgers went straight to the McAfee show and pressed “play” on his various complaints and concerns about coach Mike McCarthy.

It was specific. It was detailed. It was damning. The things Rodgers said created the clear impression that McCarthy should not be coaching the team.

This becomes a problem that goes beyond P.R. strategy. Owner Art Rooney II needs to get involved, determine whether Rodgers’s version is accurate, and take action.

It’s simple. If what Rodgers is saying is remotely true, he should not currently be the coach of the team. If Rodgers isn’t telling the truth, the Steelers need to set the record straight immediately.

However it goes, it’s a mess. A gigantic mess. An unprecedented mess for the Steelers and perhaps for any NFL franchise.

While the Bills haven’t made any official decisions on who is – or more accurately, who is not – playing tomorrow, they
sports.body: The Buffalo Bills have ruled no one out for Thursday night. The Kansas Chiefs, on the other hand, will be without two starters and a defensive depth piece come Thanksgiving night. While the Bills haven’t made any official decisions on who is – or more accurately, who is not – playing tomorrow, they do have some question marks at key positions. There aren’t any surprises, however, on the week’s final injury report. [Media: https://twitter.com/BuffaloBillsPR/status/2125660875080274406?a=8WkBYLt6AG8DoW14dd0&s=20] What we’re thinking Dalton Kincaid will be a true game time decision. A stiff ankle in the cold, or more importantly slippery wet conditions, can be concerning, but it’s something they will likely keep testing right up until 6:50 when they have to make those inactive announcements. Dorian Williams and Christian Benford, on the other hand, are more likely to be game day decisions. Soft tissue injuries aren’t fun. Rest heals them, but cold temperatures can make those muscles tense up, and cause less-than stellar play at best with a setback in recovery a likely scenario. I would think they will know early on in the day how they are feeling and if it’s safe to put them on the field. Expect to see both Tre’Davious White and Shaq Thompson called up from the practice squad again. The game time roster will probably look pretty close to identical to last week’s. And that roster wasn’t terrible. Andy Reid announced early on Wednesday that the Chiefs will be playing without Kenneth Walker III. Walker has been averaging 5.48 yards per carry and has seven touchdowns. Not the same scoring production as James Cook, but close enough to be a problem for opponents. Instead, it will be Emmett Johnson who is averaging a yard less per carry and has only touched the ball 71 times this season in the backfield for Kansas City When the Chiefs published their injury report, it also had Jaylon Moore and Omarr Norman-Lott listed as not playing. This will be third game Moore has missed with an ankle injury. Not ideal for a Chiefs offensive line tasked with keeping Greg Rousseau away from Patrick Mahomes. [Media: https://twitter.com/goldmctNFL/status/2125643394185679009?a=LkcgLByeY-golJVTHwI&s=20] As a reminder, teams are required to announce their inactive list an hour and a half before kick off. For tomorrow’s game, that means we will be checking our notifications at 6:50pm EST.

sports.title: Aaron Rodgers: Mike McCarthy fell asleep in meeting last week, broke down Steelers with "1-2-3 Packers"
sports.summary: Rodgers's first comments since being benched by the Steelers came on The Pat McAfee Show.
sports.body:
Rodgers said he did not hear the news of the quarterback change directly from McCarthy or anyone else on the coaching staff, but got the word from tight end Pat Freiermuth after it was announced on Tuesday night. Rodgers said that the change came after “months of conversation” about the offensive operation, including the playcalling, and that “things went to a different place” in recent days.

Rodgers said that McCarthy fell asleep in an quarterback meeting last Wednesday and missed other meetings leading into their loss to the Eagles on Sunday. Rodgers said McCarthy also broke down the team with “1-2-3 Packers” at halftime of that game and that McCarthy was not regularly watching film while preparing for games. Rodgers said he also believes McCarthy has lost the team in general.

Rodgers said similar things happened when the two men were with the Packers and that he believes McCarthy blames him for being fired in Green Bay after the 2018 season. He said he saw that McCarthy was not connecting with Steelers players early in training camp, but tried to help smooth things out.

“I protected him,” Rodgers said. “I didn’t talk about the things publicly. I didn’t talk about his habits.”

Rodgers also said he pushed to have changes made to the playcalling and game-planning that he believed were going to take place before Tuesday’s benching pushed things in a different direction. Rodgers said that he told the team that if they weren’t going to make those alterations that they should release him and said that there was no chance of a reconciliation with the team after how they handled things on Tuesday.

The comments guarantee that Steelers players will be asked for their accounts of how things have been in the building since McCarthy’s arrival this offseason and their responses will likely determine whether or not things go completely off the rails for the team in the final weeks of the season.

sports.title: Why tackling will be of utmost importance for Buffalo Bills vs. Chiefs on Thanksgiving
sports.summary: What do I think the biggest — and specific — defensive key for the Buffalo Bills against the Chiefs on Thanksgiving night? I’ll provide some metrics, and you’ll be able to reach the answer. The Chiefs are: and Patrick Mahomes has the: You guessed it — tackling. The Chiefs, more than any other offens
sports.body: What do I think the biggest — and specific — defensive key for the Buffalo Bills against the Chiefs on Thanksgiving night? I’ll provide some metrics, and you’ll be able to reach the answer. The Chiefs are: * First in screen-pass rate in the NFL entering this game at 16.4%, * Third in RPO rate at 8.4% and Patrick Mahomes has the: * Third-lowest average depth of target (aDOT) at 6.6 yards among 38 qualifiers * Fourth-quickest average time to attempt at 2.51 seconds among those same qualifiers * Fourth-lowest percentage of throws made 20-plus yards downfield at 9.2% among 33 qualifiers * Second-highest adjusted completion percentage at 81.1% You guessed it — tackling. The Chiefs, more than any other offense, put their opponent’s tackling capabilities to the test. How well have the Bills tackled this season, you ask? Below is a graphic that demonstrates the total amount of missed tackles credited to Bills defenders in each game by Pro Football Focus to date this season: [Image: https://platform.buffalorumblings.com/wp-content/uploads/sites/51/2026/11/correct-bills-missed-tckles-thru-wk11-1.png?quality=90&strip=all] After the bye week, which coincides with when CJ Gardner-Johnson was no longer on the team, the Bills have averaged six missed tackles per contest. In the six contests before the bye, Buffalo was averaging 8.5 missed tackles per game. Remember, before the spitting incident in Las Vegas, Gardner-Johnson was the owner of the highest missed tackle rate among qualifying safeties in the NFL. And don’t forget, on August 11, Bills defensive coordinator Jim Leonhard said the following during a press conference on this very topic: > “Who can finish, get guys on the ground? That was an Achilles’ heel here last year. So that’s the No. 1 thing we have to correct.” Per PFF, in the regular season, the Bills averaged 8.88 missed tackles per game during the 2025 campaign. In Buffalo’s two playoff outings last season, that figure jumped to 9.5 per. Right now, even with the noticeably bad start, Buffalo’s missed tackles per game average is down to 7.5. And another strong showing in the tackling department for the Bills will go a long way in securing a win over the Chiefs on Thanksgiving night.

sports.title: Buffalo Bills Week 11 game balls: Greg Rousseau and James Cook reach career milestones
sports.summary: The Buffalo Bills took care of business against the Miami Dolphins in Week 11, securing a 26-9 divisional victory at Highmark Stadium before turning their attention to a Thanksgiving night matchup with the Kansas City Chiefs. Buffalo out gained Miami 405-185, controlled the football for 36:45 and he
sports.body: The Buffalo Bills took care of business against the Miami Dolphins in Week 11, securing a 26-9 divisional victory at Highmark Stadium before turning their attention to a Thanksgiving night matchup with the Kansas City Chiefs. Buffalo out gained Miami 405-185, controlled the football for 36:45 and held the Dolphins to just two third down conversions on 14 attempts. Perhaps most impressive was the defense’s ability to keep Miami out of the end zone for all four quarters. There was plenty to celebrate in Buffalo’s locker room following Sunday’s victory, including a new career high for one defensive standout and another historic accomplishment for the Bills’ running back. Let’s take a look at who received game balls from head coach Joe Brady before handing out a few of our own. EDGE Greg Rousseau “Look, I could give this to everyone on defense the way y’all are playing right now,” Brady said before awarding his first game ball to Greg Rousseau. And rightfully so. Buffalo’s defense held Miami to just 185 total yards, 10 first downs and three field goals. But Rousseau finished the afternoon with three solo tackles, two sacks, two tackles for loss and two quarterback hits, accounting for both of Buffalo’s sacks and costing the Dolphins a combined 16 yards. His first sack came on Miami’s opening offensive possession when he brought down quarterback Kyle McCord for an eight yard loss on third and six, forcing the Dolphins to punt. With his two sack performance, Rousseau reached 10 sacks on the season, establishing a new career high with six regular season games still to play. Perhaps equally impressive is that Rousseau accomplished all of this while playing just 34 defensive snaps. RB James Cook Brady’s second game ball went to James Cook, who continues to rewrite the NFL record books. Cook finished Sunday’s contest with 22 carries for 89 yards and a touchdown. According to Brady, Cook became the first player in NFL history to record at least 75 rushing yards and a touchdown in nine consecutive games. Brady also recognized Cook for reaching 1,000 rushing yards for the fourth consecutive season. And there’s still plenty of football left to be played. What continues to impress me about Cook is his consistency. Even on an afternoon when Buffalo averaged just 3.5 yards per rushing attempt as a team, Cook found a way to produce and extend his historic streak. Sara’s Game

sports.summary: More and more information is emerging as to the surprise decision to bench Steelers quarterback Aaron Rodgers.
sports.body:
Here’s an interesting nugget, from Mike Garafolo of NFL Network.

As Garafolo explains it, the Steelers were changing their play-calling process . Starting Friday, quarterbacks coach Tom Arth, not head coach Mike McCarthy, would have been communicating the plays to Rodgers.

Previously, Arth handled play-calling during the two-minute drill. Moving forward, Arth would have been doing it for the entire game.

They worked on the new approach at practice on Tuesday. It was something Rodgers wanted.

At some point, that changed. McCarthy opted to bench Rodgers instead.

The situation dusts off the drama from nearly eight weeks ago, when Rodgers and McCarthy’s on-field unpleasantries during a loss to the Browns flowed from Rodgers’s frustrations regarding the pace of McCarthy’s play calls.

sports.summary: The sudden, late-night benching of quarterback Aaron Rodgers has created a slew of questions that are being answered in real time.
sports.body:
One of the obvious questions was answered on Wednesday morning, when Gerry Dulac of the Pittsburgh Post-Gazette reported that Rodgers didn’t show up for work on Wednesday. Implicit in that report was the idea that he chose to no-show.

Now, Adam Schefter of ESPN reports that Rodgers’s absence was “ excused ” as he processes the fact that coach Mike McCarthy has decided to play Mason Rudolph on Friday against the Broncos.

At some point, Rodgers will have something to say. Maybe he’ll make a surprise appearance on McAfee’s show today, even if that development would surprise no one.

Rodgers will surely have an opinion on the situation. Chances are that his opinion will be something other than, “You know, they were right to bench me.”

We’ve seen this movie before. Rodgers has no qualms about airing grievances. Now, the Steelers have given him a specific reason to feel aggrieved.

The surprise at this point wouldn’t be Rodgers showing up on McAfee’s show and flaming the Steelers. The surprise would be Rodgers saying nothing.

Silence could easily be interpreted as acceptance of, and possibly agreement with, the move. Beyond that, Rodgers has shown (specifically since his 2021 heel turn) that he’s never silent on topics about which he has strong feelings.

sports.body: Aaron Glenn’s first big decision when he became the New York Jets head coach was Aaron Rodgers’ future. Rodgers was interested in returning, but the feeling wasn’t mutual. AG told Rodgers to hit the road, and they parted ways. Rodgers ended up signing with the Pittsburgh Steelers, and that is where he has been since 2025. Late on Tuesday, November 24 NFL Insider Tom Pelissero revealed “The Steelers are benching Aaron Rodgers and naming Mason Rudolph the starting quarterback for Friday’s game against the Broncos. Sources say this was a coach’s decision. But Rodgers has struggled and now Mike McCarthy is making a change.” [Media: https://twitter.com/TomPelissero/status/2125442796467417433] “Aaron Rodgers will be inactive Friday, and now has potentially played the final snap of his legendary 22-year career,” Pelissero added. Now feels like a perfect time to look back and judge whether the Jets made the right decision. In 2025 the Jets finished with a 3-14 record and Justin Fields delivered an uneven season before getting benched. He started nine games, completed 62.7% of his passes, threw for 1,259 passing yards, and had seven touchdowns to one interception. He also toted the rock 71 times for 383 rushing yards and four touchdowns on the ground. Pittsburgh had a 10-7 record in 2025 and made a trip to the playoffs, but ended up losing in the wildcard round. Aaron Rodgers started 16 games last season. He completed 65.7% of his passes, threw for 3,322 passing yards and had a 24 touchdown to seven interception ratio. It seems pretty obvious that Rodgers would have been a dramatic upgrade over what the Jets trotted out at QB last year. Things in 2026 feel quite the opposite. Before Rodgers got benched he started 10 games this year. He completed 60.9% of his passes, threw for 2,241 passing yards, and had a 16 touchdown to six interception ratio. The Jets are getting much better QB play than that with Geno Smith at the helm. Smith has started all 11 games so far this season. He has completed 68.1% of his passes, has thrown for 2,402 passing yards, and has a 15 touchdown to three interception ratio. Seems like the Jets are better off with Smith in 2026 than Rodgers. sports.body: On Sunday, the Jets traveled across the country and beat the Los Angeles Chargers on the road, snapping a five-game losing streak in the process. sports.body: The calls grew loud this past week for the New York Jets to bench an injured Geno Smith and to roll with rookie quarterback Cade Klubnik. Sorry, the Jets didn’t listen. Good, because Smith delivered a spectacular showing. “Smith was nearly flawless, completing 17 of 21 passes for 176 yards and three touchdowns -- a season-high 91.4 QBR. He directed five scoring drives on the first five possessions … Counting his first go-round with New York, this was Smith’s fourth game with three touchdown passes and 80% completion rate. All other Jets quarterbacks have combined for three such games in franchise history -- Mike White, Chad Pennington and Ken O’Brien,” ESPN’s Rich Cimini wrote. If we look at Smith’s 2026 season in a vacuum, it is fantastic: 68.1% completion percentage, 2,402 passing yards, and a 15 touchdown to three interception ratio. When you compare it to the Justin Fields experience in 2025 with the Jets? It’s almost as if the two players were competing in different sports entirely. We need to start having a real conversation about 2027. No, not tanking; let’s save that for another day. I’m talking about bringing Smith back. He is scheduled to be an unrestricted free agent in 2027. Regardless of who the head coach is, they should want that kind of competency at the game’s most important position. --- J-E-T-S! sports.body: After each game, we’ll be sharing a comprehensive reivew that breaks down some of the controversial decisions from the officiating crew in the game. You may disagree in some cases, and that’s fine... Penalty Count Chargers 6-50 (leading to one Jets first down) Jets 4-18 (leading to two Chargers first downs) Note: This does not include penalties that are declined or off-set. Plays where the call was obvious, uncontroversial or not visible on broadcast footage Jets Penalties * Olu Fashanu holding on a third down incompletion in the red zone. A very clear grab by Fashanu, who pulled back on the inside of Khalil Mack’s shoulder pad as he went by him to prevent him from getting to Geno Smith. * Delay of game. Smith got frustrated here as he was unable to get everyone lined up in time and opted to just take the penalty rather than waste a timeout or rush to get the play off. Chargers Penalties * Jake Slaughter ineligible man downfield to negate a five-yard screen pass on 2nd-and-6. Clearly at least two yards downfield as the ball was being thrown, as his timing was a bit off. You only get a yard of leeway. * Delay of game on a punt. This didn’t appear to be deliberate but they had plenty of time to get it off. * Jalyn Armour-Davis was flagged for going out of bounds as a gunner on a punt. He went out without being forced by a Jets player but did make the effort to get back in the field of play which is why it was five and not 15 yards. * Donte Jackson illegal contact to negate a Chargers sack. There was a slight grab on Adonai Mitchell as he made his route break, but this was a little soft. * Ladd McConkey offensive offside and Kayode Awosika offensive holding on a red zone incompletion. McConkey was definitely on the ball, so that was clear. The hold was arguably just as clear as Awosika had a handful of Darrell Jackson’s jersey around the shoulder pad area and pulled his momentum away from pursuing the quarterback. * Cole Strange unsportsmanlike penalty after an extra point.
